executive_summary: The repository's core domain systems are healthier than the failing CI suggested. The principal issue was contract drift: recent reader, Timeline and World Map architecture changes outpaced validators and deploy assertions. This pass updates those seams while preserving substantive invariants.

open_followups.work: Continue proving parity and removing remaining legacy 3d-ui.js / 3d-selection-ui.js / old Lens-Fields-Networks compatibility assumptions one owner at a time. Do not mass-delete until unique behavior is covered by current control-plane tests.

validate_blueprints.py still reports numerous non-blocking warnings for missing implementation_notes, validation_rules and acquisition_plan. Complete these domain-by-domain rather than filling them with generic boilerplate.

Continue authored enrichment for the next critical nested Rooms: whole-body, games-simulations, visual-art, economy-finance, geography-countries, infrastructure-capability, experiments-formalization, open-questions, symbolic-body-comparison, law-justice and politics-governance.

Repository and root navigation indexes are build artifacts rather than committed source on current main. Keep builders deterministic and ensure every validator either builds prerequisites or runs only in a build stage that owns them.

Current workflows force JavaScript actions onto Node 24 because GitHub reports Node 20 deprecation. Revisit action versions when upstream releases eliminate the compatibility warning; do not churn action versions without verification.

Plans/specs are useful provenance but several describe intermediate World Map ownership states. Continue marking implementation status or linking superseding designs so historical plans are not mistaken for current architecture.

operating_rules: Validators should test canonical ownership and externally meaningful invariants, not incidental implementation strings.
A generated artifact required by a validator must be built in the same quality group before the validator runs.
Public shell/navigation contracts should derive from data/house/public-surfaces.json and current reader markers rather than parallel hand-maintained nav taxonomies.
Retired compatibility code may remain only while a documented unique behavior is still uncovered by current owners.
Warning cleanup should add real domain-specific information; never silence warnings with generic filler.
Every new high-level data subsystem should ship with a validator and be wired into one existing quality group rather than adding workflow sprawl.
